(Oakland, California) * [[San Leandro High School|San Leandro]]
([[San Leandro, California]]) | college = * {{nowrap|[[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State]] (2019–2023)}} * [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] (2023–2024) | draft_year = 2024 | career_start = 2024 | career_end = | years1 = {{nbay|2024|start}}–present | team1 = [[Miami Heat]] | years2 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2025]], [[2026-27 NBA G League season|2026]]–present | team2 = →[[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] | highlights = * [[NBA Slam Dunk Contest]] champion ([[2026 NBA All-Star Game|2026]]) }} '''Keshad Ray Johnson''' (born June 23, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Miami Heat]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA){{cite web|title=The chosen one: SDSU recruit Keshad Johnson draws strength from his brother's peril|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/sd-sp-sdsu-basketball-keshad-johnson-20181113-story.html|work=[[San Diego Union-Tribune]]|date=November 14, 2018|access-date=February 29, 2024}}{{cite web|first=Ezra|last=Amacher|title=Arizona forward Keshad Johnson signs with Miami Heat as undrafted free agent|url=https://www.azdesertswarm.com/basketball/2024/6/27/24187770/arizona-wildcats-forward-keshad-johnson-undrafted-free-agent-signing-miami-heat|work=Arizona Desert Swarm|date=June 27, 2024|access-date=June 30, 2024}}, on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State Aztecs]] and the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]]. ==Early life and high school career== Johnson grew up in [[Oakland, California]], and initially attended [[Envision Academy of Arts & Technology]].{{cite web|title=3 thoughts: San Diego State 72, San Jose State 51|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/sd-sp-sdsu-aztecs-basketball-3-thoughts-san-jose-state-20190203-story.html|work=[[San Diego Union-Tribune]]|date=February 3, 2019|access-date=February 29, 2024}} He transferred to [[San Leandro High School]] before his senior season. Johnson averaged 14.4 points, eight rebounds, three assists, 2.3 blocks and 1.9 steals per game and was named the West Alameda County Conference Foothill League co-MVP in his lone season at San Leandro.{{cite web|title=Boys basketball: Meet all-Bay Area News Group team|url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2019/03/20/boys-basketball-meet-all-bay-area-news-group-team/|work=[[The Mercury News]]|date=March 20, 2019|access-date=February 29, 2024}} He committed to playing [[college basketball]] for [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State]].{{cite web|title=The Famished Five: SDSU basketball newcomers share a hunger for success|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/story/2019-11-03/sdsu-aztecs-basketball-trey-pulliam-malachi-flynn-yanni-wetzell-kj-feagin-keshad-johnson|work=[[San Diego Union-Tribune]]|date=November 3, 2019|access-date=February 29, 2024}} ==College career== Johnson began his college career at [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State]].{{cite web|first=Jason|last=Dumas|title=Oakland native living dream of playing college basketball halted due to coronavirus|url=https://www.kron4.com/sports/oakland-native-living-dream-of-playing-college-basketball-halted-due-to-coronavirus/|website=[[KRON-TV|KRON4.com]]|date=March 23, 2020|access-date=March 3, 2024}} Johnson averaged 7.2 points and 4.5 rebounds per game as a junior.{{cite web|title=Making the grade: Aztecs basketball player Keshad Johnson flips the narrative academically|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/story/2022-06-21/san-diego-state-sdsu-aztecs-basketball-keshad-johnson-academics-gpa-west-oakland-scholar-athlete|work=[[San Diego Union-Tribune]]|date=June 21, 2022|access-date=February 21, 2024}} He averaged 7.7 points and five rebounds per game during his senior season.{{cite web|first=Hunter|last=Shelton|title=Kentucky Makes Top Five for SDSU Transfer Keshad Johnson|url=https://www.si.com/college/kentucky/mbb/kentucky-makes-top-five-sdsu-transfer-keshad-johnson|website=[[SI.com]]|date=May 6, 2023|access-date=March 3, 2024}} After the season, Johnson decided to utilize the extra year of eligibility granted to college athletes who played in the 2020 season due to [[COVID-19 pandemic]] and entered the NCAA transfer portal.{{cite web |last=Ziegler |first=Mark |date=April 12, 2023 |title=Keshad Johnson bids farewell to San Diego State |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/story/2023-04-12/san-diego-state-sdsu-aztecs-basketball-keshad-johnson-nba-draft-transfer-portal |access-date=February 28, 2024 |work=[[San Diego Union-Tribune]]}} During his 2022-2023 Senior year with SDSU, Keshad was a major contributor to the team that made the Final Four in Houston, ultimately losing in the Championship game to UConn. Johnson transferred to [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]].{{cite web |last=Tucker |first=Kyle |date=May 20, 2023 |title=Top-10 transfer Keshad Johnson chooses Arizona, leaving Kentucky in need of talent |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4537869/2023/05/20/kentucky-arizona-keshad-johnson/ |access-date=February 21, 2024 |work=[[The Athletic]] |via=The New York Times}} He averaged 11.5 points, 5.9 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 0.7 blocks and 1.0 steals per game.{{cite news|first=Cyro|last=Choch|title=Keshad Johnson: NBA draft scouting report and intel|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2024/05/27/keshad-johnson-nba-draft-scouting-report-and-intel/73872026007/|work=[[USA Today]]|date=May 27, 2024|access-date=July 14, 2024}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Johnson signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Miami Heat]] on July 1, 2024{{cite web|title=HEAT SIGN KESHAD JOHNSON TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-keshad-johnson-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2024|access-date=July 1, 2024}} and joined them for the [[2024 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Hanifan|title=Miami Heat announce 2024 Summer League roster|url=https://hothothoops.com/2024/07/03/miami-heat-announce-2024-summer-league-roster/|website=HotHotHoops.com|date=July 3, 2024|access-date=December 26, 2024}} On December 26, he signed a standard contract with the Heat{{cite web|title=HEAT SIGN KESHAD JOHNSON|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-keshad-johnson|website=NBA.com|date=December 26, 2024|access-date=December 26, 2024}} and on January 24, 2025, he was [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] to the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].{{cite web |title=2024-2025 Sioux Falls Skyforce Transaction History |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Sioux-Falls-Skyforce/6/Transaction_History/2025 |access-date=February 2, 2025 |website=RealGM.com}} Johnson won the [[Slam Dunk Contest]] during the [[2026 NBA All-Star Game|2026 NBA All-Star Weekend]].{{cite web|title=Heat’s Keshad Johnson soars to a slam dunk title, edging Carter Bryant who had a perfect score|url=https://apnews.com/article/nba-all-star-dunk-contest-ec62b646e2015d761ded3838fa990858|access-date=February 14, 2026|website=apnews.com}} He was noted for his various dance moves he performed between dunks.
